item.title: Indian-origin man stopped and questioned over immigration status in Chicago; governor says it was ‘because of his skin color’
item.description: An Indian-origin US citizen, working for Illinois DOT, was questioned by masked federal agents about his immigration status and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Governor Pritzker condemned the incident as potential racial profiling. The Department of Homeland Security denied the agents were from ICE or CBP, but the event caused local alarm and school lockdowns.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Hundreds of cops resign ahead of Zohran Mamdani’s term in NYC: ‘How do you work for a mayor who wants to defund police?’
item.description: New York City is experiencing a significant increase in police officer departures, with a 35% rise in October, as morale plummets ahead of Mayor-elect Zohran Mamdani's inauguration. Union leaders express concern over Mamdani's proposed reforms, fearing they will exacerbate attrition and make the job unsustainable for remaining officers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: JD Vance hopes his Indian-Hindu wife will convert to Christianity — experts weigh in on interfaith marriage
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance sparked controversy by expressing hope his Hindu wife, Usha Vance, might convert to Christianity. While Vance converted to Catholicism, he stated his wife has free will. Experts weighed in on interfaith marriage, emphasizing respect and open dialogue, with some criticizing Vance's remarks as reflecting a singular path to salvation.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Steve Bannon trolled after saying Republicans will go to prison if GOP loses 2028 elections; ‘Weird thing to admit but okay’
item.description: Steve Bannon's dire prediction of imprisonment for MAGA activists if Democrats win in 2028 has sparked widespread online mockery. Critics derided his warning as an admission of guilt and compared it to a villain's monologue. Bannon's recent focus on 2028 and Trump's potential third term has further fueled online ridicule, overshadowing his alarmist message.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Epstein scandal: Ghislaine Maxwell is enjoying ‘happier time, VIP experience’ in new prison, says report
item.description: Ghislaine Maxwell describes her new Texas prison as safer and cleaner than her previous Florida facility, praising improved conditions. However, lawmakers are investigating allegations of special treatment, including special meals and private showers, sparking anger among other inmates and community members.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Why is the Moon slowly moving away from Earth every year and what does it reveal about our planet’s future
item.description: Our Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth, not just due to tidal friction as previously thought. New research suggests ancient planetary impacts and Earth's internal cooling, causing contraction and faster rotation, are also significant drivers. This complex interplay reshapes our cosmic relationship and offers insights into other planetary systems.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Mystery deepens: Interstellar object 3I/ATLAS shows no comet tail and leaves scientists stunned
item.description: Interstellar object 3I/ATLAS has surprised scientists by showing no cometary tail after passing close to the Sun. This unexpected behavior challenges the assumption that it's a typical comet, fueling debate about its origin and the formation of objects from other star systems. Further observations are planned to unravel its true nature.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: ‘You work for us, not billionaires’: Joe Biden fires fresh salvos at Donald Trump, slams his ‘golden age’ claim
item.description: Former US President Joe Biden strongly criticised Donald Trump in Omaha. Biden accused Trump of damaging America's institutions and mocked his White House renovations. He stated Trump's actions went beyond expectations. Biden also highlighted the importance of affordable healthcare. He celebrated recent Democratic victories, seeing them as a rejection of Trump's agenda. Biden urged unity to protect democracy.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: YouTuber Candace Owens fires back at Ben Shapiro after he claims she accused Erika Kirk of killing Charlie Kirk
item.description: Candace Owens vehemently denied accusing Erika Kirk of her husband Charlie Kirk's death, calling Ben Shapiro a liar for his claims on The Megyn Kelly Show. Owens stated Shapiro fabricated the accusation to discredit her. Meanwhile, Erika Kirk appealed for public grace following her husband's passing, emphasizing the impact of online discourse on her children.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Meet Felicette: France’s first cat in space and historic feline astronaut
item.description: In 1963, France launched Félicette, the first cat into space aboard a Véronique AGI 47 rocket. Her 13-minute suborbital flight provided valuable data on weightlessness and neurological activity. Félicette's mission marked a significant milestone for France in early animal space exploration.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Zohran Mamdani’s wife Rama Duwaji faces fire over her 'Israeli war crimes' artwork: 'Mourns deaths of terrorists'
item.description: Incoming New York First Lady Rama Duwaji, an artist, has consistently voiced strong political stances through her work, particularly concerning US foreign policy and Israel's actions in Gaza. Her art critiques American imperialism and highlights alleged deliberate starvation in Palestine. Duwaji, whose family has humanitarian ties, aims to use her voice as a US citizen to speak out against injustices.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kuwait Airways flight KU417 delayed after minor Tarmac incident at Kuwait Airport
item.description: A Kuwait Airways flight to the Philippines experienced a significant delay early Friday morning due to a technical glitch involving the aircraft's brake system. The incident, which occurred on the tarmac before takeoff, caused minor damage to the fuselage but no injuries to the 284 passengers or crew.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Better work on your H-1B visa’: MAGA supporters grill Vivek Ramaswamy after Trump backs his Ohio governor bid
item.description: Vivek Ramaswamy thanked Donald Trump for his gubernatorial endorsement, but online reactions revealed divisions within the Republican base. Trump praised Ramaswamy as "Young, Strong, and Smart" and urged unity, highlighting shared priorities. Despite a clear Republican field, Ramaswamy faces a general election challenge in 2026.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Row erupts over Sydney Sweeney’s response on ‘white supremacy’ in American Eagle ad: ‘She’s always been a MAGA’
item.description: Sydney Sweeney's recent interview reignited controversy surrounding an American Eagle denim campaign. The advert, featuring the tagline "Sydney Sweeney Has Great Jeans," faced accusations of racism and eugenics.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: If you fell into a black hole, would you survive? What new research says about spaghettification
item.description: Falling into a black hole means facing extreme stretching, known as spaghettification, due to immense tidal forces. While supermassive black holes might allow crossing the event horizon intact, destruction is inevitable near the singularity. Scientists study this process to test physics boundaries and understand cosmic events, revealing insights into gravity and information paradoxes.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Did Zohran Mamdani do a ‘Nazi salute’? Social media compares his wave to Elon Musk, calls out ‘double standards’
item.description: Newly elected NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani sparked an online debate after a video of his victory speech went viral. Critics claimed his arm-waving gesture resembled a Nazi salute, drawing comparisons to a similar controversy involving Elon Musk. The incident reignited discussions about public behavior, symbolism, and political intent.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE: Fujairah tightens hiking rules with mandatory certified guides and expanded penalties
item.description: Fujairah is professionalizing its adventure tourism sector with a new policy requiring certified mountain guides for all treks. This initiative aims to enhance safety, protect lives, and create an organized environment for visitors. A digital platform will support route registration, best practices, and accredited training, empowering local guides and ensuring robust insurance for operators.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Sudan: One-sided truce prompts calls for humanitarian aid
item.description: Sudan's Rapid Support Forces have agreed to a three-month humanitarian truce. This move follows ongoing violence and a severe humanitarian crisis. The truce, proposed by the Quad countries, aims to pave the way for a ceasefire and political process. However, concerns persist regarding the RSF's commitment and past actions.

item.title: Denmark to ban social media for children under 15
item.description: Denmark is implementing a minimum age of 15 for certain social media platforms to protect youth mental health, following Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's call for restrictions. The country is allocating significant funds to enhance online child protection and strengthen EU's Digital Services Act supervision.

item.title: Shein avoids ban in France — government
item.description: France will not ban online retailer Shein during an investigation into illegal items, as the company has removed all such products from its platform. While legal proceedings continue and the firm remains under close observation, authorities found no child pornography, stabbing weapons, or certain medicines being sold.
